item.title: DHS defends ICE shooting in NYC, says officers believed they were in danger
item.description:
Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) released new details Friday about the shooting of an illegal immigrant with a rap sheet who had long been on the run. ICE officers were making their second attempt to arrest 28-year-old Oscar Belgal, who had fled from them in September, when they shot him Thursday afternoon in New York City, agency officials said during a press conference on Friday. Belgal, who had a 5-year-old child in the car, refused orders to exit after officers boxed him in, then accelerated and struck two ICE vehicles, said Marcos Charles, executive associate director of ICE’s Enforcement and Removal Operations (ERO). item.title: How the oil industry is preparing for Hurricane Isaias
item.description:
The hurricane approaching the northern Gulf Coast has been upgraded to a major Category 3 with maximum sustained winds of 120 mph — and it threatens to bring heavy rain, severe flooding, tornadoes, and power outages to the western Florida Panhandle, Alabama, Mississippi, and other parts of the Southeast. Hurricane Isaias, the first of the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season, is set to make landfall near the Pensacola, Florida, area Friday evening with a life-threatening storm surge of up to 9 feet. Coastal Alabama to Port St. Joe could also see 5 to 7 feet. Forecasters expect some weakening before the hurricane hits land, but warn Isaias will remain dangerous regardless of its exact strength. Mandatory evacuation orders have been issued for several coastal counties. item.description:
Hammam al-Hammami is believed to have been targeting the passenger terminal at Ben Gurion airport near Tel Aviv The co-pilot who tried to seize control of a passenger jet flying from Dubai to Tel Aviv last week was planning to launch a suicide attack targeting the passenger terminal at Israel’s international airport, prosecutors in the United Arab Emirates said on Friday. Hammam al-Hammami attacked the plane’s Indian pilot with an emergency axe, but failed to prevent his badly injured colleague from opening the cockpit’s security door to allow passengers to overpower his assailant. item.title: How Hurricane Isaias broke through to become the first Atlantic hurricane in an eerily quiet 2026 season
item.description:
Owners of an ice cream shop board up their windows in Gulf Breeze, Fla., on Oct. 8, 2026, ahead of Hurricane Isaias. Joe Raedle/Getty Images Hurricane Isaias shattered the peace of one of the quietest Atlantic hurricane seasons on record as it grew into 2026’s first Atlantic hurricane and headed for the northern Gulf Coast , with landfall expected late on Oct. 9 or early Oct. 10. Coastal residents and store owners in Alabama and the Florida Panhandle quickly began boarding up windows and preparing sandbags for damaging wind, rain and storm surge. Tyndall Air Force Base, which suffered severe hurricane damage in 2018, started evacuating fighter jets . Isaias tied a 1905 storm for the latest-forming first hurricane of a season on record. item.title: Prediction Markets Have a Lock on the Midterms
item.description:
As so-called prediction markets like Kalshi and Polymarket embed themselves in every aspect of our daily lives, from elections to sports and entertainment, concerns have grown about what the explosion of these poorly understood, loosely regulated platforms could mean for regular people and democracy writ large. Celebrities from LeBron James to Sydney Sweeney have inked lucrative deals with prediction platforms. Legacy news outlets have even begun including prediction market data in their coverage. And the Trump family is deeply embedded in these platforms’ success; Donald Trump Jr.’s VC firm just became a lead investor in Polymarket, and he is a paid adviser to both Polymarket and Kalshi. But what actually is a prediction market, and what separates it from online sports betting platforms like DraftKings or FanDuel?
